quizzes.title: DevOps & Cloud Computing Fundamentals
quizzes.description: Test your core knowledge on CI/CD pipelines, containerization, Kubernetes, and Cloud Run.

questions.text: What does CI/CD stand for in modern software engineering?
questions.explanation: CI/CD stands for Continuous Integration (automated building and testing) and Continuous Deployment/Delivery (automated releasing to production).

questions.text: Which tool provides lightweight container virtualization using images and layers?
questions.explanation: Docker packages applications and dependencies into standard container images sharing the host OS kernel.

questions.text: In Kubernetes, what is the smallest deployable computing unit that encapsulates one or more containers?
questions.explanation: A Pod is the basic execution unit in Kubernetes, hosting one or more containers sharing storage and network namespaces.

questions.text: What is the primary benefit of Infrastructure as Code (IaC)?
options: Running servers without an operating system
Managing and provisioning infrastructure via declarative version-controlled files
Replacing all backend code with SQL queries
Eliminating the need for unit testing
questions.explanation: IaC allows infrastructure specifications to be documented, automated, version-controlled, and audited just like software code.

questions.text: Which Google Cloud service is a fully managed serverless platform for deploying containerized apps?
questions.explanation: Cloud Run is Google Cloud's serverless runtime that automatically scales stateless containers up or down to zero.

quizzes.title: Python Programming & FastAPI Mastery
quizzes.description: Evaluate your understanding of Python syntax, async/await, Pydantic schemas, and FastAPI conventions.

questions.text: Which library does FastAPI use for high-performance data validation and typing?
questions.explanation: FastAPI is built tightly with Pydantic for data validation, serialization, and automatic OpenAPI documentation generation.

questions.text: In Python, which keywords are used to define and execute asynchronous coroutines?
questions.explanation: 'async def' declares an asynchronous function and 'await' pauses execution until the awaited awaitable completes.

questions.text: What does the 'pass' statement do in Python?
options: Acts as a syntactical placeholder statement that does nothing
Throws an exception to pass control up the stack
Skips the rest of the loop iteration
questions.explanation: 'pass' is a null operation in Python used when a statement is required syntactically but no code needs to execute.

questions.text: What ASGI server is standardly paired with FastAPI for production serving?
questions.explanation: Uvicorn is a lightning-fast ASGI server implementation, using uvloop and httptools to run async Python applications.

questions.text: Which Python decorator is used in FastAPI to define a GET endpoint on a router?
questions.explanation: FastAPI uses HTTP-verb decorators like @router.get() or @app.get() to define path operations.

quizzes.title: Web Architecture & HTTP Protocols
quizzes.description: Essential knowledge covering HTTP status codes, RESTful methods, React fundamentals, and JWT auth.

questions.text: What HTTP status code represents '401 Unauthorized'?
options: The client is authenticated but lacks permission
Authentication credentials are required and either missing or invalid
The requested resource was permanently moved
The server encountered an unhandled internal exception
questions.explanation: HTTP 401 Unauthorized indicates that the request has not been applied because it lacks valid authentication credentials.

questions.text: Which HTTP method should be used when submitting answers to create a new quiz attempt?
questions.explanation: POST is used to submit an entity to the specified resource, commonly causing a change in state or creating a subordinate resource.

questions.text: In React, which hook is used to perform side effects like fetching data or synchronizing with external APIs?
questions.explanation: useEffect lets you perform side effects such as data fetching, timers, and manual DOM mutations after rendering.

questions.text: What does CORS stand for in browser web security?
questions.explanation: CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) is an HTTP-header based mechanism enabling a server to indicate any origins other than its own from which a browser should permit loading resources.

questions.text: How many parts separated by dots (.) does a standard JSON Web Token (JWT) contain?
questions.explanation: A JWT consists of three parts separated by dots: Header, Payload, and Signature, formatted as header.payload.signature.
